newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: U.S. accuses Croatia of crimes against refugees.
newsitem.headline: U.S. accuses Croatia of crimes against refugees.

text.p: John Kornblum, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for European Affairs, accused Croatian leaders on Monday of failing to protect refugees from ethnic minorities returning to their homes.

Kornblum appealed at a U.N. humanitarian meeting in Geneva for Croatia to end intimidation against minority refugees returning under last year's U.S.-brokered Dayton peace accord which ended 43 months of war in former Yugoslavia.
"Croatian authorities have failed to protect the victims and have often perpetrated the crimes," he said in his speech, a copy of which was made available by the U.S. mission.
"These heinous acts send a chilling message to those who remain in eastern Slavonia and to those who might return to other parts of Croatia."
Kornblum added: "Zagreb must end this intimidation. The international community will hold the government of Croatia accountable for failure."
Eastern Slavonia is a Serb-held Croatian enclave bordering the Yugoslav republic of Serbia and is due to return to Zagreb's control.
Thousands of people were killed or expelled from the region, which saw some of the worst fighting in the war sparked by Croatia's bid for independence from Yugoslavia.
The U.N. Security Council in November extended its 5,000-strong peacekeeping mission in Eastern Slavonia until the middle of 1997. Elections in the area are expected to be held in April.
Kornblum said much still had to be done under the Dayton accord.
He said only 250,000 displaced Bosnians had so far gone home out of 870,000 initially hoped for when Dayton was agreed.
"Even more troubling, more than 90,000 people who were in their residences a year ago have fled," Kornblum said.
Nearly two million people remain displaced a year after the signing of the Dayton peace accord.
